summary: Pin production Helm images and restrict daemon pod identity and filesystem defaults
details: Use one validated image selection for API, worker and migration pods. Production requires a lowercase SHA-256 digest; structured image.digest and existing tag@digest values are supported, with conflicting selections rejected.

Create separate release/component daemon ServiceAccounts, disable automatic Kubernetes API tokens on accounts and pods, add scoped provider-identity annotations and shared pre-provisioned image-pull Secret references without RBAC grants.

Default to numeric non-root UID/GID 10001 and read-only roots with existing seccomp/capability/escalation guards. Give daemons bounded disk-backed /tmp scratch and ephemeral-storage budgets; production rejects relaxed declared guards and filesystem object storage.
Scope pod labels, the API Service and the optional starter ingress policy to the Helm release while preserving immutable Deployment selectors for upgrades.

Exercise immutable image selection, private-file validation, component identities, scratch, long release names and production guard failures through rendered manifests and actual native startup input checks.

compatibility.notes: Production tag-only chart values must add a digest; existing digest-qualified tags continue to work. Tag-only development images require env.production=false. Pod identity/filesystem defaults require compatible mounted-file permissions; custom container security fields are limited to the declared chart interface. Deployment selectors remain unchanged, while the documented stop/drain upgrade replaces pods with new release labels and accounts. Existing runtime credential Secret fallback behavior is preserved.

security: The chart enforces immutable image selection, bounded scratch and declared production pod guards, with tokenless component identities and release-specific traffic selection. Digests do not establish publisher authenticity, ServiceAccounts create no provider grants, and render checks do not prove cluster admission or network enforcement.
limitations: Runtime credential separation and the remaining network/disruption/runbook work remain in EVY-1206. The starter ingress policy is still optional; this unit does not claim complete deployment hardening.
Live container/cluster filesystem and identity rehearsals, plus required full-ticket migration/deployment/restore/production/final gates, remain pending until ticket readiness.
